_doc.value: Machine-readable half of the SOUL rules. The argument lives in the §; the number lives here. Change both together (sk-improve), then lint every video. Every key is { value, rule, why }. These are defaults measured on one channel; re-measure yours.
_doc.why: one source of truth for numbers, so code never hard-codes a threshold

maxDurationSeconds.why: hard platform ceiling: a YouTube upload over 3 minutes is not a Short (a 195.5 s video was published as a regular video)

targetDurationSeconds.why: soft pacing target; past ~90 s the edit starts to drag unless the content earns it

outroHoldSeconds.why: silent hold on the last frame so the viewer has a beat to share; a missing default once cut four videos at the last word

maxWordsPerSentence.why: mechanism sentences with but/because/so run up to ~25 words; longer ones need a full stop. Measured in a syllable-counted language: re-measure for yours

medianWordsPerSentence.why: median of 1,266 Shorts sentences from six large knowledge channels; much lower medians read as a summary, not a person who knows

shortSentenceMaxShare.why: sentences of 7 words or fewer are about 1 in 8 on large channels; a run of them sounds flat and machine-written

shortSentenceMaxWords.why: the length that counts as 'short' for shortSentenceMaxShare

veryShortSentenceMaxShare.why: sentences of 4 words or fewer are about 1 in 25 on large channels, and still have a subject and a verb

factEverySeconds.why: about one information beat per 2.5 s keeps a 70-80 s video above 25 beats; does not apply to things that must be read

readingHoldSeconds.why: a frame shown for 3.8 s drew 'the images flash by too fast'; comparing takes longer than looking

onFrameTextMaxSceneShare.why: more than half the scenes with on-frame text is a sign of failure; viewers remember none of seven valid headlines

kickerMaxChars.why: a kicker is a label, read in one glance

headlineMaxWords.why: a headline that is a sentence belongs to the voice; the frame carries data

longSceneSpokenSeconds.why: past this, ledger details should move from the voice to the frame

captionWordsPerChunk.why: captions follow the ear; whole sentences on screen are a wall of text

captionBottomShare.why: caption block bottom ~24% of frame height above the bottom edge, clear of platform UI

safeLandscapeMarginPct.why: 16:9 has no platform button column; keep text inside the classic 5% title-safe margin so TVs and players that overscan do not cut it

captionBottomShareLandscape.why: on a 1080-high frame the portrait 24% would put captions in the middle of the picture

captionMaxWidthLandscapePx.why: a caption line wider than ~73% of a 1920 frame forces the eye to travel; two to four words per chunk stay short anyway

safeTopPx.why: strictest top UI edge (Reels) on a 1080x1920 frame

safeRightPx.why: strictest right button column: x from Reels, start height from TikTok

panelMaxWidthPx.why: a centred panel wider than this pokes into the button column; size for the final camera scale

captionSecondLangMaxLines.why: a third line of the translation overlaps the main caption silently

captionSecondLangMaxChars.why: about two lines at ~30 px inside the panel width

promoLoudnessLUFS.why: a film with no voice to protect sits lower than a voiced short; the source TVC mixed at about -16.7 LUFS integrated

promoTruePeakMaxDb.why: AAC overshoots 0.2 to 0.6 dB after encode, so leave margin under the -1 dBTP ceiling

promoMaxDurationSeconds.why: a promo that needs more than 90 s is two films; lint warns above it, it is not a platform limit

loudnessLUFS.why: raw renders sit near -20 LUFS and play quieter than the rest of the feed; re-measure after encode

truePeakMaxDb.why: never clip; the platform re-encode adds overshoot

uploadTruePeakMaxDb.why: the ceiling on the encoded upload file: normalize aims lower (truePeakMaxDb, promoTruePeakMaxDb) and AAC can overshoot by 0.2 to 0.6 dB; encode fails above this

musicUnderVoiceDb.why: floor for P90 minus P10 of 200 ms RMS windows on the encoded file; below it the bed swallows the voice. Narrow is not bad by itself (the best video sat at 12.1). Warn only

musicFadeOutSeconds.why: an even fade to zero before the silent hold

sfxMaxPerVideo.why: SFX are accents; scattered evenly they turn an explainer into a meme video

sfxTargetLUFS.why: SFX files varied by 11 dB; normalize each just under the voice

audioSampleRate.why: unusual rates (96 kHz) are mishandled by uploaders

strongWords.why: off by default; a channel may allow one strong word as an accent. More than one turns the accent into the voice. Never in title, description, cover or on-frame text

value: at the end of the day
bannedPhrases.why: hype, essay joints and trailer wrapping: the places where channels sound identical. Large channels use each in 0-4% of videos

intensifiers.why: an adjective the viewer cannot check, next to a real number, weakens the number

intensifiersMax.why: one emphasis per video keeps it meaningful

hookOnlyPhrases.why: long-lived channels greet and ask to subscribe mid-video; only the first seconds are too expensive for it

bannedMarks.why: spoken text becomes captions; these read as an outline and create no pause for the voice

silentPunctuation.why: the pause pipeline only breaks on . ! ? ; these marks create zero silence

maxSilentInLongSentence.why: a sentence already over the limit that leans on commas means the writer thought the comma made a pause

pronounOpeners.why: the first sentence of each scene names its subject; mid-scene pronouns are fine

repeatGramSize.why: four-word phrases are long enough to be a mould, short enough to catch one forming

repeatGramMinVideos.why: a phrase in 3+ videos is a mould forming ('reason number one' grew into seven videos unnoticed); share scene and flow markers exempt

recapMinScenes.why: a payoff sharing distinct four-word phrases with 2+ body scenes is recapping. Warn only (it can be a deliberate callback)

sourceOnlyEndings.why: a sentence that ends on a reporting verb usually carries nothing but its source; matching the ending is narrower than matching words

maxDatesPerScene.why: p90 of the source channel; three or four dates in a scene is telling by chronology instead of story

maxDatesPerVideo.why: p90 of the source channel across 46 scripts

maxParallelRun.why: three consecutive sentences opening with the same word are an outline in story costume

universalWords.why: a scene resting only on single-study or review evidence may not speak for all of humanity

weakEvidenceLevels.why: evidence levels that do not allow universal words

coverCropRatio.why: profile grids crop 1080x1920 to ~1:1.29, losing 263 px top and bottom

coverGridWidthPx.why: the cover is ~200 px wide in the grid: one number and about three words survive

descriptionFirstLineMaxChars.why: the first line becomes the YouTube title, capped at 100 characters

descriptionMaxChars.why: platform caption cap; hashtags count toward it

footageFillers.why: single-word filler sounds `bun run cut` proposes to remove; a phrase filler ("kiểu là", "you know") is a judgement, cut it by hand

footageMaxGapSeconds.why: every silence between kept words is shortened to this; longer reads as a stall on a phone, shorter swallows breaths and sounds spliced

footagePadSeconds.why: air kept around each kept run so a cut never clips the first or last syllable

footageRetakeWindowWords.why: a restart of the same three words within this many words is proposed as a retake (the last attempt is kept)

footageLowConfidence.why: Whisper words under this confidence are flagged with ? in the review: likely misheard names and numbers

footageJoinMaxDb.why: a join louder than this cuts through a syllable; the same quiet threshold `bun run tts` uses between lines (§4)

footageCtaPhrases.why: a filmed video that ends on a call to action ends on a logo in words; cut to the turn

footageFaceMarginPx.why: an effect whose top edge is less than this above the declared face band would hang over the face; lint knows only top edges, the still review checks the rest

effectsPerMinute.why: shared effects (caption, marks, chart) per minute of a talking-head video: fewer is a static selfie, more is noise over the person

punchEffectsMax.why: WordSlam and Stamp are the exclamation mark; a second one in the same video cancels the first

footageClipRetakeShare.why: a filmed clip whose three-word runs are mostly said again in a later clip is a re-take of it; the later clip is kept

footageClipRetakeMinWords.why: below this many words two clips share too few runs to call one a re-take of the other

vi: cảm ơn các bạn đã theo dõi
hẹn gặp lại các bạn trong những video tiếp theo

whisperHallucinations.why: phrases Whisper invents over silence or noise; on the first multi-clip test it wrote 'Hãy subscribe cho kênh Ghiền Mì Gõ' over a clip that never said it. Words in them are marked unsure so the speaker confirms them

sentenceOpeners.why: a transcript with no full stops is split into lines at these words when capitalised, even right after a name ("Sài Gòn Thì …"); names never are
